# Document DockLayouts styling, themes, and action chrome

## Context

DockLayouts styling now spans an engine affordance floor, registered theme identities, dock preview sheets, inline tab headers, action rails, splitters, rails, and Workstation-specific token values. Recent fixes repeatedly showed that correct component ownership does not guarantee correct CSS cascade authority.

## The Problem

The Adoption guide says “skin it with tokens,” but does not teach the full layering model or how to verify it. Consumers can accidentally copy engine paint, lose popup-vessel token reach, create equal-specificity property conflicts, or make focus/overflow action chrome visually unstable.

## The Architectural Reality

`resources/scss/src/dashboard/**` owns structural paint and neutral `--dock-*` consumption. Theme trees provide registered defaults/accents. App sheets such as Workstation set values and deliberate density policy. Tab-header/action chrome crosses shared tab/toolbar primitives while floating overflow menus and popup vessels have separate embodiment scopes.

## The Fix

Create `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsStyling.md`: a visual-language guide explaining engine floor versus theme versus app skin, token reach across vessels, inline header/action composition, and computed-style verification.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Styling guide | Current SCSS structural/theme/app layers | Teach ownership and token flow without copying declaration catalogs | Re-census at pickup | New guide | Computed-style + screenshot receipts |
| Floating embodiments | Current overflow/popup/reveal implementations | Explain token reach across body/window scopes | Name honest limits | Same guide | Workstation + standalone consumers |
| Registration | Existing guide siblings | One discoverable UI-building-blocks guide | No generated-output edits | tree + SEO inputs | lint + rendered portal |

## Decision Record impact

## Decision Record

Not needed; this guide explains presentation layering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guide clears the full guide-authoring bar: source/tool-grounded narrative, reader-owned benefits, lived maintainer voice, and at least one render-verified `flowchart TD`.
- [ ] The guide separates explanation from reference: no inlined API/schema/test catalog, and no ticket or PR ids in guide prose.
- [ ] The new source guide is registered in `learn/tree.json` and the SEO `PRIORITIES` input; generated sitemap/LLM outputs remain untouched.
- [ ] Current-source consistency, guide lint, tree lint, portal rendering, and an independent cross-family whole-guide review are recorded in the PR.
- [ ] The guide distinguishes engine structural paint, registered theme values, and app-owned token values/density deviations.
- [ ] Inline tab headers, overflow-first/close-last action chrome, rails, splitters, previews, reveal controls, menus, and popup vessels are grounded in current rendered consumers.
- [ ] Computed-style and screenshot receipts cover every registered Engine theme relevant at authoring time plus Workstation palettes; no hard-coded theme count.
- [ ] Specificity and inheritance are explained through one real failure-and-fix story, not a selector catalog.

## Out of Scope

Redesigning the visual language, relocating SCSS, or duplicating the generic Styling and Theming guide.

## Avoided Traps

Do not move app identity into engine defaults, treat selector presence as paint ownership, hand-edit generated CSS, or infer cascade correctness from SCSS source alone.

## Activation Gate

Do not author the guide while #17836 remains an active refactoring authority. At pickup, re-run Memory Core mining, read the current ADR 0029 and source/test surfaces named below, exercise the relevant live subsystem, and revalidate the proposed guide boundary. If the final API makes this split wrong, reshape this ticket before writing—do not preserve a stale outline.
